level_title: Final Raid: Ignis-Py, The Guardian of Pythonia

questions.title: Stage I • Phase 1: Forging the Obsidian Ward (Variables & Type Casting)
questions.prompt: [STAGE I: THE OBSIDIAN SHIELD] Ignis-Py hurls a wave of Molten Syntax! Convert the string mana scroll "450" into an integer so it can be added to your base shield of 550!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard says: To add a numeric string like "450" to an integer, wrap it in Python's 'int()' type-casting function!
questions.explanation: Shield forged! 'int("450")' converts the string "450" into the integer 450, so 550 + 450 = 1000 Ward Power!

questions.title: Stage I • Phase 2: Piercing the Magma Scales (Conditionals & Lists)
questions.prompt: [STAGE I: THE OBSIDIAN SHIELD] Ignis-Py shifts his elemental scales! What value is stored in 'spell' after this conditional check runs on the 'scales' list?
questions.hint: Archivist Venn says: Check both sides of 'and': '"obsidian" in scales' is True, and 'len(scales) == 3' is also True!
questions.explanation: Direct hit! Because "obsidian" is inside the 'scales' list AND its length is 3, the 'if' branch executes and assigns "glacier_lance"!

questions.title: Stage II • Phase 3: [DEBUG MODE] Defusing the Corrupted Loop Curse!
questions.prompt: [STAGE II: OVERDRIVE & CORRUPTION] Ignis-Py corrupted your spell-charging loop with a bug! Click the ONE line of code that contains the error preventing 'total_dmg' from accumulating each hit!
questions.code_snippet:
# BUG HUNT: Find the corrupted line in this loop!
damages = [20, 30, 50]
total_dmg = 0
for hit in damages:
    total_dmg = hit
fire_beam(total_dmg)
questions.hint: Master PyWizard says: Look inside the 'for' loop body—using '=' overwrites 'total_dmg' each iteration instead of adding to it with '+='!
questions.explanation: Curse defused! Changing 'total_dmg = hit' to 'total_dmg += hit' accumulates 20 + 30 + 50 = 100 damage instead of overwriting it!

questions.title: Stage II • Phase 4: Invoking Weaver Sera's Relic Function (def & return)
questions.prompt: [STAGE II: OVERDRIVE & CORRUPTION] Weaver Sera lends her Arcane Obelisk! Complete the keyword inside 'forge_lance' so the function sends the computed damage back to the caller.
questions.code_snippet:
def forge_lance(base, mult):
    power = base * mult
    ____ power

strike = forge_lance(125, 2)
questions.hint: Weaver Sera says: A Python function uses the 'return' keyword to output its result back to the variable that called it!
questions.explanation: Obelisk beam fired! 'return power' sends 250 back to 'strike', shattering Ignis-Py's volcanic wing armor!

questions.title: Stage II • Phase 5: [DEBUG MODE] Fixing the Guardian's Matrix Trap!
questions.prompt: [STAGE II: OVERDRIVE & CORRUPTION] Scribe Kael warns you: Ignis-Py planted an off-by-one IndexError trap in your targeting script! Click the line that causes an IndexError or logic bug!
questions.code_snippet:
# BUG HUNT: Target the FIRST and LAST cores in the 3-item list!
cores = ["ruby", "topaz", "diamond"]
first_core = cores[0]
last_core = cores[3]
shatter(first_core, last_core)
bug_lines: last_core = cores[3]    # <-- Index 3 is out of range!
questions.hint: Scribe Kael says: A 3-element list only has indices 0, 1, and 2 (or -1 for the last item). Accessing 'cores[3]' triggers an IndexError!
questions.explanation: Trap shattered! In a 3-item list, valid indices are 0, 1, 2 (or -1). Replacing 'cores[3]' with 'cores[-1]' safely locks onto "diamond"!

questions.title: Stage III • Final Phase: The Grandmaster Synthesis Finisher!
questions.prompt: [STAGE III: GRAND SYNTHESIS] All 4 Mentors channel their power into your staff! Arrange the Python blocks to define 'grand_finisher(runes)', loop over the list, and return the combined power!
questions.code_snippet: # Assemble the Complete Python Function, For-Loop, and Return Statement
questions.hint: Master PyWizard says: Start with 'def grand_finisher(runes):', initialize 'power = 0' and start the 'for' loop, check 'if r > 0:', and finally 'return power'!
questions.explanation: GRANDMASTER VICTORY! You synthesized Variables, Conditionals, Loops, Functions, and Lists to vanquish Ignis-Py and become the Grand Champion of Pythonia!
